text:
Alex P.: Quick sync — we need a concrete prioritization for private packaging connectivity (VPC peering, transit VPN, on-prem overlay) by EOD Fri. Biggest asks from field: stable egress IPs, minimal network ops, and an upgrade story with <1h downtime.
Mira G.: Agenda: 1) customer-impacting constraints 2) engineering feasibility 3) launch gates 4) action owners. Can we list top 5 customers and their constraints here? @Leila (CS)
Leila (CS): Top 5: AcmeBank (regulatory, strict egress IP allowlist), HealthCo (airgapped + HSM), RetailHub (multi-tenant VPC, wants peering), AdScale (can use outbound-only NAT), GovDept (requires on-prem + no inbound). All asked for clear upgrade rollback paths.
Chris R.: Engineering notes: supporting both peering and transit VPN increases surface area but doable. Key tradeoffs:
- VPC peering: easiest latency, needs CIDR management, no transitive routing.
- Transit VPN (IPSec): supports isolation, more ops, NAT handling.
- Overlay (wireguard/mesh): works for on-prem but adds agent lifecycle.
We need to pick a primary path for GA.
Jon (Eng): If we pick peering as GA, we must support: predictable advertised IPs, NAT fallback, and a canary upgrade with dual-stack container images. Effort: ~6w to implement peering + rollout automation, ~4w for VPN, ~3w for agent overlay (but agent testing longer).
Sam T.: Security checklist: mutual TLS for control plane, KMS integration for keys, audit logs for handshake events, no inbound unless explicit customer opt-in. For peering customers we need documented ACLs and optional NAT gateway config.
Alex P.: Launch gates proposal:
- Gate A: docs + customer runbook (must)
- Gate B: 2 pilot customers on chosen path (peering or VPN)
- Gate C: rollback tested (DB failover + config rollback)
- Gate D: compliance signoff for customers with regulated data
If any gate fails -> delay GA. Thoughts?
Mira G.: LGTM. Suggest we add an interoperability gate: ability to fallback to hosted model variant in case of network failure (auto-route to regional hosted). That keeps app live.
Chris R.: Technical caveat: fallback requires prefix/CIDR translation and token scoping; adds ~1w effort but is high value.
Leila (CS): Customers will pay premium for stable IP + migration help. Request: include an "upgrade assist" professional services checklist for first 10 customers.
DevOpsBot: deploy-notify: created ticket INF-3245 for peering automation epic.
Alex P.: Decision proposal (vote):
- GA primary path = VPC peering with documented NAT fallback
- Secondary: transit VPN for customers who can't peer
- Agent overlay reserved for airgapped/offline installs (post-GA)
Please react with :thumbsup: to approve or :eyes: to flag concerns. Deadline EOD Fri.
Jon (Eng): :thumbsup: from eng side — will scope detailed tasks tomorrow.
Sam T.: :thumbsup: assuming KMS + mTLS are in the plan.
Mira G.: :eyes: request one more data point: estimated rollback SLO for upgrades (target <1h). Can eng commit?
Chris R.: We can aim for <1h rollback for config-only changes; full DB migrations will be out-of-scope for GA. We'll document constraints.
Leila (CS): :thumbsup: from CS, but add customer comms templates to the runbook.
Alex P.: Next steps:
- @Jon (Eng) create task breakdown under INF-3245 by EOD Tue
- @Mira G. draft pilot criteria + success metrics (latency, failover)
- @Leila (CS) collect pilot customers and prepare PS checklist
- @Sam T. start security checklist + KMS integration plan
I'll collate and publish a short decision memo after Friday. Thanks everyone.

```
  type: vpc-peering
  allowed_cidrs: ["10.0.0.0/16"]
  advertise_ips: ["203.0.113.45"]
  nat_fallback: true
```
End of thread.
